small_guidance:
- The kernel currently launches grid (N, OUT_HW/BLOCK_M) and iterates over all OC tiles inside a single program; this serializes the OC sweep and prevents the SM from hiding latency. Add OC tiling to the grid (N, OUT_HW/BLOCK_M, OC/BLOCK_N) and do the channel-min via atomic-min or a two-pass reduction; or fuse partial mins across CTAs using a small post-reduction kernel.
- Expand autotune with larger BLOCK_M (128-256) paired with BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=16 and num_warps=8, num_stages=2 — verify (BM·BK+BK·BN)·4·stages ≲ 132KB. Also try BLOCK_K=64 with smaller BLOCK_M to amortize weight-load latency for IC=64.
- Inside the inner loop, precompute the base x and w pointers per (kh,kw) and hoist `ih*W*IC` out of BLOCK_K loop; also load the full IC=64 in one shot (BLOCK_K=64, NUM_K_TILES=1) to remove the inner kt loop entirely.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a persistent im2col GEMM with the channel-min fused as the epilogue across the full OC dimension within one program: one program owns a spatial tile of BLOCK_M outputs for a single (N), streams through all OC in BLOCK_N chunks while keeping the GEMM-K accumulator resident, and maintains a running min vector of length BLOCK_M in registers. This avoids needing inter-CTA reduction while still parallelizing spatial tiles.
- Alternatively split into two kernels: (1) a tuned NHWC conv GEMM producing (N, OH, OW, OC) in fp32, (2) a channel-reduction kernel doing min+scale. This separates concerns and lets the conv kernel use a standard 2D-tiled (M=spatial, N=OC) GEMM with BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32. Memory traffic of the intermediate (64·128·254·254·4 ≈ 2GB) is large, so prefer the fused persistent design above unless OC tiling on the grid is added.
- Consider implicit-GEMM with the input stationary in shared memory across kh,kw (load a (BLOCK_M_spatial + KH-1) × IC halo tile once per program), which cuts redundant x loads by a factor of KH·KW=9 — the current kernel reloads x for every (kh,kw) pair.
